run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T06:34:44Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on frontend-proxy is explained by HTTP 504 responses that frontend-proxy returns after its ~15s upstream timeout: the retrieved 504 traces are POST /api/checkout requests whose latency is dominated by checkout's Kafka publish span 'orders publish' of 14.99s and 15.58s, while every other span in the same traces completed in sub-100ms. That publish latency was <=2ms per span in the 06:10-06:30 baseline and became 10-30s in 06:37-06:47 (164 of 255 spans above 15s), immediately after the kafka Deployment replaced its broker pod at 2026-11-17T06:32:13Z; checkout logged connection refused to kafka:9092 from 06:32:59 to 06:33:47 and the new broker auto-created the 'orders' topic at 06:33:51. The alerting signal (frontend-proxy ingress STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans) began deviating in the 06:28:44-06:33:44 window (6.7 -> 26.7 per 5m) and peaked at 116.7 per 5m at 06:42:44. The frontend-proxy, checkout and kafka pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts and low CPU (checkout ~0.01 cores, kafka ~0.02-0.05 cores with ~0.8-1.4% CFS throttling after the restart), and the consumer side (accounting, fraud-detection) processed orders with all spans <=1s. The kafka Deployment's pod template was unchanged apart from the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt annotation and the broker has no persistent volume, so broker and topic state was discarded and re-created. Hypothesis, not established: that broker state loss caused checkout's producer to block 10-30s per publish, which exceeded frontend-proxy's 15s route timeout. A second candidate, the flagd-config setting kafkaQueueProblems='on' (declared as overloading the Kafka queue and adding a consumer-side delay), is reported only as a hypothesis because the declared consumer-side delay was not observed and the flag's change time cannot be determined.

claims.text: frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR were 0-7 per 5m between 06:16:44 and 06:32:44, then 26.67 at 06:33:44, 42.22 at the 06:34:44 alert time, and peaked at 116.67 at 06:42:44; total ingress spans fell from about 3,800 per 5m to about 2,000-3,300 per 5m over the same interval.

The frontend-proxy error spans are HTTP 504 with error=true and otel.status_code=ERROR, each about 15,000,000 microseconds (15s) long; their child 'router frontend egress' spans carry error="true" and http.status_code="0" and last about 15s, i.e. frontend-proxy's upstream call timed out and no response was received.

Two complete 504 traces (trace_ids d3066bd6d4294c09a9c14e1f7b11fd20 and 78b0cd23085487069ee05cd833880f28) both carry load-generator operation user_checkout_single: frontend POST /api/checkout 15.01-15.72s and checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 15.01-15.72s, dominated by checkout span 'orders publish' of 14.99s and 15.58s, while payment Charge is 0.3-35.9ms, currency Convert <=2ms, product-catalog GetProduct <=1ms, shipping <=85ms, email <=4ms, cart <=2.3ms and quote ~0.3ms.

checkout's own log lines for the Kafka publish show 'Successful to write message. offset: 0, duration:' values of 11.27s, 10.67s, 11.36s, 10.43s, 8.95s, 10.11s, 9.83s, 10.37s, 14.43s, 13.80s, 26.31s, 28.71s, 31.20s, 29.83s, 32.33s and 31.80s between 06:35:49 and 06:36:29, and 8.79-29.48s between 06:39:23 and 06:41:54.

Checkout span 'orders publish' had a fast baseline: in 06:10-06:30 the le=2.0 bucket equals the +Inf bucket (388-411 spans per 10m), whereas in 06:37-06:47 the +Inf bucket is 255.4 spans, le=10000.0 is 6.3 and le=15000.0 is 91.4, so about 164 of 255 publishes exceeded 15s and almost none were under 10s.

checkout logged 'Failed to connect to broker kafka:9092: dial tcp 100.65.62.181:9092: connect: connection refused' and 'Failed to write message: ... circuit breaker is open' repeatedly from 06:32:59 to 06:33:47, then 'Connected to broker at kafka:9092 (unregistered)' and 'client/brokers registered new broker #1 at kafka:9092' at 06:33:58.

The kafka ReplicaSet pod template carries kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T06:32:13Z; new ReplicaSet kafka-5c9d7cc485 was scaled 0->1 and pod kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 created at 06:32:13-06:32:14 while old ReplicaSet kafka-ff7884766 was scaled 1->0 and pod kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2 was killed at 06:32:15 (ScalingReplicaSet, SuccessfulCreate and SuccessfulDelete events).

The old and new kafka ReplicaSet pod templates are identical (same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-kafka, same env including KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS=PLAINTEXT://kafka:9092, same limits cpu 400m and memory 900Mi) except for the added kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt annotation on the new ReplicaSet; the kafka pod's only volume is kube-api-access, i.e. the broker has no persistent volume.

After the replacement the new kafka broker auto-created the topic orders: 'CreateTopics result(s): CreatableTopic(name=orders, numPartitions=1, replicationFactor=1 ...): SUCCESS' at 06:33:51, followed by 'Creating new partition orders-0' and 'Created log for partition orders-0' at 06:33:54 with initial high watermark 0.

The checkout span 'orders publish' had STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans only in the step ending 06:35 (increase 22.9 per 5m) and 0 in the steps ending 06:40 and 06:50, matching the 06:32:59-06:33:58 broker-unreachable period; afterwards publishes logged by checkout and recorded by spans succeed but take 10-30s.

After the restart the kafka container used only about 0.02-0.05 CPU cores with 0.8-1.4% CFS throttling at 06:41-06:45, its JVM cpu utilization ratio was about 0.0005, and its limits are 400m CPU and 900Mi memory; the checkout container used about 0.01 cores with 0% throttling under a 250m/512Mi limit; neither was CPU-throttled during the 10-30s publishes.
The kafka Service has exactly one endpoint, 100.96.4.3 ports 9092 and 9093, targeting pod kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97, and checkout's KAFKA_ADDR is kafka:9092.

The consumer side was not slow: at 06:47 accounting 'order-consumed' spans were 110.3 of 255.4 <=1000ms and 238.5 of 255.4 <=5000ms (baseline 06:25: 191.6 of 403.2 <=1000ms and 391.6 of 403.2 <=5000ms), and fraud-detection 'orders receive' and 'orders process' were all 255.4 spans <=1000ms at both times.

The ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config enables a fault-style flag: kafkaQueueProblems has defaultVariant "on" (variants off:0, on:100), state ENABLED, description "Overloads Kafka queue while simultaneously introducing a consumer side delay leading to a lag spike"; every other flag in that ConfigMap (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) has defaultVariant "off".

Error-span counts per 10m at the 06:37:23 step were frontend-proxy 65.3, checkout 16.2, ad 1.05 and recommendation 1.05 (both unchanged at 1.05 in the 06:17:23 and 06:27:23 steps), and 0 for frontend, payment, accounting and fraud-detection.

All 21 otel-demo pods are Running and Ready with 0 restarts except fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-zcxzm (restartCount 2, last termination OOMKilled, exitCode 137), whose events are BackOff at 06:25:19 and Started at 06:25:32, before both the kafka pod replacement (06:32:13) and the frontend-proxy error deviation (06:33:44).

The kafkaQueueProblems flag's declared 'consumer side delay' was not observed: accounting and fraud-detection consumer spans stayed <=1000ms (accounting at most 6.7% of spans above 5000ms) after the incident, so the flag's declared consumer-side effect does not match the observed producer-side publish stall.

frontend-proxy is not itself starved or failing: its pod is Ready with 0 restarts, uses about 0.014-0.025 cores with 2.8-4.6% CFS throttling, and its 504 is produced after 15s on an upstream call whose child span carries http.status_code=0, while the frontend handler behind it completed the request with HTTP 200 at 14.97-15.72s.

Kafka broker CPU exhaustion cannot explain the publish latency: at 06:41-06:45 the kafka container used only about 0.02-0.05 cores with about 0.8-1.4% CFS throttling and a JVM cpu utilization ratio of about 0.0005, while about 164 of 255 checkout 'orders publish' spans exceeded 15s.

The kafka Deployment's broker pod replacement at 06:32:13 discarded the broker's non-persistent state (no PVC, kube-api-access volume only), forcing re-creation of the orders topic at 06:33:51 and a reset producer/broker session; checkout's Kafka publish then blocked 10-30s per message, pushing POST /api/checkout past frontend-proxy's 15s upstream timeout and producing the 504s behind the alert. The causal link is inferred from tight timing, not from a broker-side measurement.

The kafkaQueueProblems fault flag set to 'on' in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config is the injected cause of the Kafka publish latency. Supporting: it is the only fault-declaring setting enabled in the otel-demo ConfigMaps and its description concerns overloading the Kafka queue and a lag spike. Against: the observed consumer-side path is fast, consumed message counts equal checkout's publish counts (no overload), and the pre-06:32 baseline publish latency was <=2ms, so the flag cannot be shown to have been active for the whole period.

An unobserved stall on the path between checkout and kafka (node disk I/O for the broker's /tmp log, or pod-network packet loss or retransmission) delays produce acknowledgements while the broker stays idle at about 0.02-0.05 CPU; the available metric names include no node disk or pod network series, so this can be neither confirmed nor excluded.

frontend-proxy itself is failing or overloaded: rejected, because its 504 spans are its own timeout after 15.001s on a 'router frontend egress' span with http.status_code=0, the frontend returned HTTP 200 at 14.97-15.72s, the only slow span is checkout 'orders publish', and the pod is Ready with 0 restarts and low CPU.

The fraud-detection OOMKilled restarts caused this alert: rejected, because its BackOff and Started events are at 06:25:19-06:25:32, before the kafka pod replacement (06:32:13) and before the frontend-proxy error deviation (06:33:44), its error-span count is 0, and its orders-consumer spans were all <=1000ms.

A downstream checkout dependency (payment, currency, product-catalog, cart, shipping, quote, email) is the cause: rejected, because inside the 504 traces those calls completed in sub-100ms with gRPC status 0 or HTTP 200, and payment, frontend, accounting and fraud-detection had 0 error spans per 10m.

Verify whether the kafkaQueueProblems flag is intended to be on; if not, set defaultVariant back to "off" in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config, restart the flagd pod so the mounted config is reloaded, and then re-check checkout 'orders publish' latency and the frontend-proxy 504 rate.

Establish who applied kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T06:32:13Z to the kafka ReplicaSet template and why; since the broker pod carries no persistent volume, a restart discards broker and topic state, so give the log directory a PVC if restart survivability is required.

Because the broker is idle while produce calls take 10-30s, collect broker-side request-queue and produce timing, node disk I/O series, and checkout's Kafka client debug logs (or a packet capture on the checkout-to-kafka path) to locate where the publish time is spent.

gaps: No change_history integration is available, so when the flagd-config kafkaQueueProblems flag changed to "on", and what or who triggered the kafka rollout restart (restartedAt 2026-11-17T06:32:13Z), cannot be determined.

The flagd queries returned no data: logs for pod flagd-f546d44c9-zx5qq over 05:34:44-06:47:23 returned 0 lines from init-config, flagd and flagd-ui (view status no_data), so a flag reload or change event could not be observed.

No kafka broker request-level, node disk or pod network metrics exist among the 63 metric names in the target Prometheus (none matched disk or network series), so the reason checkout's produce calls take 10-30s while the broker is idle at about 0.02-0.05 cores and about 1.4% throttling remains unexplained.
The kafka container's log output ends at 06:41:42, so broker behaviour after that is unknown.

list_prometheus_rules for RequestErrorRate returned no data (view status no_data), so the alert's exact PromQL expression and the annotation value current: 0.4 could not be verified; the measured 5m error share of frontend-proxy ingress spans at 06:34:44 was about 1.2%.

The cluster-wide query for NetworkPolicy objects returned no objects (view status no_data) and the Istio CRD query returned none (view status no_data); whether any external policy could affect the checkout-to-kafka path could not be verified. Pods in otel-demo each carry a single container, so a meshed sidecar fault injection in the pods was not present.

Traces are a sampled view and the Redis and Postgres backends of cart and accounting were only observed indirectly through their service spans; slow requests that did not reach the 15s timeout were not enumerated.

Fault-declaring settings outside the otel-demo ConfigMaps were only searched by object name and CRD name (no chaos CRDs exist), so other injection mechanisms outside the read kinds cannot be excluded.
next_steps: Ask the platform or change owner why the kafka workload's pods were rolled at 2026-11-17T06:32:13Z and whether the flagd kafkaQueueProblems flag was toggled around the same time.

If the flag is the intended fault injection, turn kafkaQueueProblems off and re-measure checkout 'orders publish' span latency and frontend-proxy ingress STATUS_CODE_ERROR to confirm or refute the hypothesis.
Add broker-side (request queue, ack) and node disk and network telemetry so the next occurrence can distinguish a broker-state effect from an I/O or network stall.
Consider persisting the kafka log directory on a PVC so that a broker pod replacement does not delete topics such as orders.
